common_name: Beatrice Haddrell Begonia (Dark Star-Shaped Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; a longtime favorite among rhizomatous begonia collectors for its easy nature.

directions: Pot in a light, fast-draining, humus-rich mix and grow in bright, indirect light out of direct sun, which fades the leaf color. Beatrice Haddrell forms a mounding clump of spiky, star-shaped leaves in near-black burgundy-brown with a bright green star radiating from the center of each leaf, a bold contrast pattern that has made it an old favorite among rhizomatous begonia growers. Pale pink flowers appear above the foliage in late winter into spring, though the plant is grown chiefly for its leaf pattern. Let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings and divide the creeping rhizome at repotting time to produce new plants.
sources: American Begonia Society rhizomatous begonia references

common_name: Helen Teupel Rex Begonia (Heirloom Violet-Red Pointed-Leaf Rex Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; one of the older, easier-to-grow Rex begonia hybrids, dating to the late 1920s.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix, keeping soil evenly moist but never waterlogged, since Rex begonia rhizomes rot quickly in soggy conditions. Helen Teupel is a classic heirloom Rex begonia hybrid with non-spiraling, pointed maroon leaves splashed with pink and silver toward the margin, carried on red, hair-covered petioles, and is considered one of the easier older Rex cultivars for a beginning grower to succeed with. Pale pink flowers appear occasionally but are secondary to the foliage display. Maintain elevated humidity, let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings, and divide the rhizome at repotting time to propagate new plants.

common_name: Bunny Hug Begonia (Small Silver Textured Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; keep slightly snug in its pot, since Bunny Hug flowers best when a little pot-bound.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light in a humus-rich, fast-draining mix, keeping the plant a little snug in its pot to encourage flowering. Bunny Hug bears small, silver, textured leaves no more than two inches across, lightly covered in fine hairs and tinged with a soft pink blush, a full, compact habit that makes it noticeably easier to grow than many other silver-leaved rhizomatous begonias. White flowers appear on long, slender stems above the foliage in spring. Provide slightly higher humidity than typical houseplants need, let the topsoil dry between waterings, and divide the rhizome to propagate.
sources: American Begonia Society rhizomatous begonia references

common_name: Caribbean Prince Begonia (Trailing Khaki-and-Red Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; the tight trailing habit suits a hanging basket better than an upright pot.

directions: Grow in partial to full shade in a humus-rich, well-drained mix, ideally in a hanging basket where the tight trailing stems can cascade. Caribbean Prince is a compact, vigorous rhizomatous begonia with textured, khaki-green leaves that flush red underneath and shift through aqua, ochre, and umber tones with the seasons and light, giving the plant a constantly changing look. Sweet-scented white flowers with pink buds appear mainly in winter but can recur through the year. Let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings and divide the rhizome at repotting time to produce new plants.
sources: American Begonia Society rhizomatous begonia references

common_name: Deco Checks Begonia (Checkered Green-and-Russet Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; give a minimum of about 60F, since cooler temperatures can cause leaf problems.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light in a well-drained, humus-rich mix, keeping temperatures above about 60F to avoid leaf damage. Deco Checks is a popular modern rhizomatous begonia whose avocado-green leaves develop bold brown and russet checkered markings as they age, starting bright green on young growth and deepening into a distinctive patchwork pattern over time. Its compact, tidy growth habit makes it easier to keep shapely than many patterned rhizomatous types. Let the mix dry between waterings, fertilize lightly once or twice a month during active growth, and divide the rhizome to propagate.
sources: Carter & Holmes Orchids — Begonia Deco Checks

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; leaf color shifts with the season and light level, so rotate the pot occasionally for even coloring.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light in a humus-rich, well-drained mix; Earthtones is a compact, full-growing rhizomatous begonia with rounded, slightly lobed leaves on stiff, upright petioles. Its name comes from the leaf color, which shifts with the season and light level through shades of aqua, ochre, and raw umber, each leaf marked with darker veining and spotting. Bright, hot-pink flowers appear above the foliage in spring. Let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings and divide the rhizome at repotting time to produce new plants.
sources: American Begonia Society rhizomatous begonia references

common_name: Harmony's Stormy Sunset Begonia (Pink-to-Silver Tear-Leaf Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; a sport of the cultivar 'Passing Storm' with a looser, more open mounding habit.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light in a humus-rich, well-drained mix, allowing the soil to become fairly dry between waterings. Harmony's Stormy Sunset is a sport of the rhizomatous begonia 'Passing Storm', with tear-shaped leaves that emerge soft pink and gradually age to a shimmering silvery grey, veined in grey-green, giving the plant an ever-changing two-tone look as new and older leaves mix in the loose mound. Light pink flowers appear above the foliage in season. Divide the rhizome at repotting time to produce new plants and keep the clump vigorous.
sources: Kartuz Greenhouses — Begonia Harmony's Stormy Sunset

common_name: Indian Summer Begonia (Velvety Russet-and-Olive Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light, which deepens the leaf coloring; avoid direct sun, which can scorch the velvety surface.

directions: Pot in a light, fast-draining, humus-rich mix and grow in bright, indirect light, which brings out the richest leaf color. Indian Summer carries broad, lobed, star-shaped leaves with a velvety sheen, shifting seasonally between russet, amber, and deep olive tones around a glowing central eye and red central veins, with a softly serrated, hairy edge. The medium-sized rounded leaves give it a warmer, earthier palette than silver- or variegated-leaf rhizomatous types. Let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings and divide the creeping rhizome at repotting time to propagate new plants.
sources: American Begonia Society rhizomatous begonia references

common_name: Kingsbury Begonia (Upright Blue-Green Angular-Leaf Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; an older, rarely offered hybrid dating to the early 1960s that takes some training to grow into a shapely plant.

directions: Grow in bright, filtered light in a humus-rich, well-drained mix, since Kingsbury's upright rhizome needs a bit more grooming than trailing rhizomatous types to stay shapely. Its angular, jagged-edged leaves carry a distinctive blue-green tinge and are fringed with fine red hairs along the margin, with a crest of red color at the base of each petiole. Pink flowers appear above the foliage in spring. Let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings and divide the rhizome at repotting time to produce new plants.
sources: American Begonia Society rhizomatous begonia references
